item.title: Trump Says U.S. Military Campaign to Wind Down and Plans National Address
item.summary: “We will be leaving very soon,” the president told reporters in the Oval Office. A few hours later, the White House said Mr. Trump would provide “an important update on Iran” on Wednesday evening.

item.title: Europe Has a ‘Guns vs. Butter’ Problem. War in Iran Makes It Worse.
item.summary: After decades of prioritizing domestic over military spending, the continent’s leaders are trying to pivot. That is straining national budgets and could anger voters.

item.title: King Charles to Visit U.S. as Tensions Rise Between Trump and Britain
item.summary: President Trump has fired criticism at America’s longtime ally over the war in Iran, but there are hopes that the royal visit will help shore up relations.

item.title: How the U.K.’s Leader Decides Which U.S. Bombers to Let Fly Against Iran
item.summary: As the United States expands its armada of warplanes on British soil, Prime Minister Keir Starmer says he is trying to defend Britain’s interests while keeping the country out of war.

item.title: Israel Passes Law to Hang Palestinians Convicted of Deadly Attacks
item.summary: Experts say the law was written in such a way as to ensure that it was unlikely to ever apply to Jewish extremists who commit similar crimes.

item.title: Israel’s Message to Southern Lebanon: Shiites Must Go
item.summary: Israel has issued sweeping evacuation warnings, and pressed some Christian and Druse leaders to expel Shiite Muslims from their towns, the leaders said.

item.title: 29 Killed in Russian Military Plane Crash in Crimea
item.summary: Investigators cited a possible technical malfunction.

item.title: Israelis Prepare to Celebrate Passover in Shadow of War
item.summary: The atmosphere during preparations for the Jewish festival has been unusually subdued, with people afraid to stray far from their homes and shelters.

item.title: U.S. Senators Press Taiwan to Raise Military Spending, as China Protests
item.summary: Four visiting senators urged Taiwan to break an impasse over a $40 billion budget proposal, highlighting concerns in Washington about the threat from China.

item.title: U.S. Plans Military Expansion in Greenland
item.summary: The Pentagon is in talks with Denmark for access to three more areas on the Arctic island. Several Greenlanders said they didn’t like the idea.
